title: How WebAssembly Executes

content.explanation: JavaScript and WebAssembly use different execution pipelines inside browsers. JavaScript goes through parsing, bytecode generation, and optimization. WebAssembly arrives as binary instructions and goes through validation and compilation. Although their paths differ, both eventually become machine code executed by the CPU. This shared destination allows both technologies to work together efficiently.
content.example: A JavaScript application can call a WebAssembly function for heavy calculations.
content.analogy: Two roads from different cities leading to the same destination.
content.keyTakeaway: JavaScript and WebAssembly follow different paths to machine code.

revisionSummary: Different pipelines reach the same CPU.
